subject: order factors of a mixed-number-letter type

messages.author: db582c6760911594
messages.subject: order factors of a mixed-number-letter type
parts:
Hello, I am qplot-ting 1-dimensional quantitative data that is grouped
according to the names of mouse chromosomes. Their names are of mixed
type - letters and characters - 1, 2, 3....19, X, Y. For publication,
I need to get the plotting of the groups in this order.:
1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ......, 19, X, Y.

After struggling with conversions between factors and characters which
did not help I invented a small trick. I managed to get the proper
ordering by replacing the names of chromosome X and Y with numbers 20
and 21:

qplot(y=as.numeric(as.character(quantitative_values)),x=factor(x,
levels=c(1:21)),data=data_frame, geom = "jitter")

but now, after they are plotted in the right order, I need to rename
the 20 and 21 back to X and Y.

Is it possible to set the names of the x axis tick marks?

Regards, Radek

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: order factors of a mixed-number-letter type
parts:
Hi Radek,

You'll find it much easier to just set the levels of the factor to the
correct order. e.g.

df$x <- factor(df$x, levels = c(1:19, "X", "Y"))

Hadley

Hadley, don't you have to also add ordered=T?

vals <- c(1:19, 19, 19, "X", "Y")
d <- factor(vals, levels = c(1:19, "X", "Y"))

> is.ordered(d)
[1] FALSE

I would have thought this would work better:

> d <- factor(vals, levels = c(1:19, "X", "Y"), ordered=T)
> is.ordered(d)
[1] TRUE

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: order factors of a mixed-number-letter type
parts: > Hadley, don't you have to also add ordered=T?

Nope. Technically ggplot2 should use this information (mainly for
colour & shape scales), but it doesn't matter for position.

Hadley

--
http://had.co.nz/

messages.author: 262bfcbf6d4ecc3a
messages.subject: Re: order factors of a mixed-number-letter type
parts:
Yes, be careful adding ordered = T. For example, lmer will switch you
from standard contrasts to polynomial ones if you make ordered true.
Most software (all?) uses the order of the level regardless of whether
the factor is officially an ordered factor.

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: order factors of a mixed-number-letter type
parts:
Interesting; I find that non-intuitive. For example I would have
thought that a program would be ok to optimize something else in a
graph or analysis by varying order, if the factor was not specified to
be ordered (e.g. by using an unordered hash table data structure in
preparing the analysis). Good to know that it can sometimes be a
hazard and isn't needed for ggplot2, which uses the implicit semantics
of the order of the array used to define the order of the levels.

Setting the factor order directly in the data frame works perfectly
and seems very elegant to me. You just have to watch out for unwanted
changes during merging etc. of the data frames and re-set the factor
order if changed. Radek
